narrative: Seven tickets across ten months, each in a different module, with no repeat defects and an even, unremarkable tone throughout. The one open item, a report builder crash on a 40-field template ('the report builder to freeze and eventually crash the browser tab'), was never revisited. Reads as normal product use, not a relationship at risk.

Connector sync frequency and alert delivery both recur after being marked fixed: the customer notes the connector fix 'was apparently fixed but looking at the logs it's still only syncing twice a day,' and alerts fail again, 'the second time in six weeks.' By January the tone turns explicit: 'The pattern here is clear and it's not acceptable,' and by February, 'I don't know what else to say at this point.' The final dashboard 'no data' ticket is left unresolved with no further contact. This is a chronic-reliability account with visible loss of patience across two named contacts.
Two straightforward how-to questions four months apart, both resolved quickly with no friction. No signal of risk in this account.

Seven distinct issues over a year (encoding, formatting, timeouts, sync lag), each resolved, with only one repeat: Nordic character encoding, fixed once then recurring on a different export a month later, then resolved. Tone is matter-of-fact throughout with no pattern of accumulating unresolved friction.

competitor_mentions.quote: We looked at Dashlume a while back partly on API limits, so it would help to get clarity on what our Standard plan actually allows before we plan next quarter's integration work.

narrative: Single ticket about API rate limits, resolved. Mentions having 'looked at Dashlume a while back' as context for a planning question, a passing reference rather than active procurement. No other signal in the record.

Three tickets nine months apart, calm and low-volume. The most recent, a webhook that 'hasn't fired despite a couple of changes' with a direct question on whether it's actually supported, sits unresolved with no follow-up yet. Too sparse and too mild to call deteriorating, but worth a check-in on the webhook.
Five distinct, resolved issues over eight months, even tone throughout, no repeats. Healthy account showing routine day-to-day use.

Export timeouts and failures recur repeatedly across sixteen months: flagged in October, again in February ('same pattern as what we reported in October... thought this was resolved'), again in May ('third time we've raised this exact issue... why a fix that was confirmed twice hasn't held'), and again in August, where the ticket text shrinks to 'Fourth time. No further comment.' That terseness after three prior rounds of explanation reads as resignation, not resolution, the underlying export defect has never actually held. Routine admin tickets continue afterward, but the core reliability problem the customer has raised four times is still open.

Only three tickets in fourteen months, but the pattern is the quiet, worrying kind: an export-formatting bug recurs two months after being 'fixed,' and rather than escalate, the customer reports they've 'settled into just reformatting in Excel each time before it goes out... so there's no pressing need to escalate,' while noting 'the earlier fix doesn't appear to have addressed the underlying cause.' A customer building a permanent manual workaround around an unfixed defect, and explicitly choosing not to escalate, is a classic quiet-erosion signal despite the low ticket count.
Six varied, resolved issues over a year, no repeats, no tension in the language. Healthy account.
Two isolated issues six months apart, both resolved without friction. No signal of risk in this account.

Nine tickets over almost two years mixing compliments ('loving the new update'), feature requests, and smooth onboarding ('better than we expected... thanks for the extra support call'). Every issue resolves cleanly and the customer keeps expanding usage with a new ERP connector, custom roles, and digest requests. This is an engaged, growing account.
Four distinct, resolved issues over a year: token TTL, a cosmetic connector duplicate, an access-log request, a broken embed, with even tone throughout. No repeats, no accumulating friction.

competitor_mentions.quote: we've had Dashlume's API demoed to us recently as part of a wider systems review, so keen to compare properly before committing further engineering time either way
given it's a new integration built specifically around comparing favourably against Dashlume's offering, it would be good to see it stabilise properly at some point

narrative: The account is actively benchmarking Kataja against a named competitor: 'we've had Dashlume's API demoed to us recently as part of a wider systems review, so keen to compare properly before committing further engineering time.' A month later they describe the very integration built for that comparison as unstable, 'some days it pulls correctly, others it silently returns partial data with no error.' They aren't escalating, they've added their own row-count check and say they're 'not chasing this hard,' but they are quietly benchmarking a competitor against an integration that doesn't fully work yet, which is a materially different risk than a routine bug.
Four routine issues across seven months, all resolved, no repeats, no tension in the language. Healthy account.

Extremely high ticket volume (19 tickets over 18 months) with consistently blunt language ('Please just fix it,' 'not exactly confidence-inspiring'), but every issue gets fixed within a day or two and the account keeps returning to use the product hard across every module, including for board meetings and CFO reporting. The exception is exports, which fail with the same symptoms repeatedly across the whole period, blank files, missing columns, wrong currency, timeouts, corruption, right through to the final ticket in October 2025 ('Blank export, here we go again. Same as always'), plus a connector outage that recurred three days after being 'fixed.' The loud tone reads as an engaged, heavy user frustrated by persistently unfixed modules rather than a customer preparing to leave.

A working cross-datasource join stops functioning in March 2025 and stays broken through three follow-up tickets: 'we've heard nothing in six days... now going on two weeks.' A second system, the CRM connector, then fails on top of it, with the customer stating plainly 'usage of the platform across our team has dropped significantly because people can't trust the data' and demanding 'a senior contact to own these issues.' Two core issues are unresolved at the end of the record with an explicit statement of reduced platform trust and usage, the clearest failing-relationship signal in this batch.

A rough first year, report builder breakage, silent alerts, an admin-roles bug that never got 'properly closed out,' then API instability on top of it, escalates in December to 'this needs to go above the support queue... we need a call with account management.' After that call, every subsequent ticket reports genuine improvement: 'most things have been noticeably steadier,' 'the API has been solid for a few weeks,' 'alerts have been reliable for a while now, good change from last year,' plus positive feature-building tickets. One report builder template still throws an occasional error as of March 2025 but is described as 'smaller than before.' This is the escalation-then-recovery arc: real risk a year ago, genuinely resolved since.

A report builder export button that does nothing goes unresolved, but the same ticket notes a working alternative ('works fine from the regular export menu elsewhere'), so it reads as a minor irritant rather than a blocker. Five months later the account is calmly setting up a new connector for a newly added subsidiary, expansion, not disengagement.

Two minor bugs (a stuck alert field, an overlapping chart legend) are reported within the same month and never followed up on, then a nine-month gap before two ordinary, resolved questions. The silence on the first two issues could mean either indifference or quiet abandonment of those features, but there is no tonal sign of frustration and usage continues normally afterward.
